title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock
gist: Dalia Marin links the AfD's near-majority 43.8% win in Saxony-Anhalt's September 6, 2026 election to Germany's 'China shock': competition from China is breaking the postwar bargain in which high-value manufacturing delivered good jobs, export revenue and social cohesion.

insights.claim: In the September 6, 2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election, the far-right AfD won 43.8% of the vote, more than twice its 2021 share, and came within three seats of an absolute majority.
insights.speaker: DALIA MARIN
insights.so_what: A far-right path to outright state government is now plausible, raising German political-risk premia and questions about governability.

insights.claim: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU, the incumbent governing party in Saxony-Anhalt, collapsed to 17.2% from 37.1% in 2021.
insights.speaker: DALIA MARIN
insights.so_what: Erosion of the centre-right weakens Merz's federal mandate for reforms and fiscal plans; watch coalition stability.

insights.claim: The Saxony-Anhalt election could mark a turning point in Germany's postwar political history.
insights.speaker: DALIA MARIN
insights.so_what: Signals structural, not cyclical, political realignment in Germany, relevant to European policy outlook and Bund/euro risk.
insights.quote: could mark a turning point in Germany’s postwar political history

insights.claim: Germany's postwar stability rested on an implicit bargain in which high-value manufacturing provided good jobs, strong export revenue and broad prosperity, which political institutions turned into social cohesion.
insights.speaker: DALIA MARIN
insights.so_what: Understanding the bargain explains why industrial decline translates directly into political instability in Germany.

insights.claim: Competition from China is shaking Germany's manufacturing-based social bargain to its foundations and contributing to the rise of the AfD.
insights.speaker: DALIA MARIN
insights.so_what: Pressure on German industrial exporters (autos, machinery) is a political as well as earnings risk; expect protectionist/industrial-policy responses.
insights.quote: Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.
